title: Define service lifecycle ownership and recovery contracts
goal: Make install/update/uninstall eligibility and uncertain-operation recovery explicit before any existing installation or OS service changes
acceptance: Validate selected installation, current and legacy definitions, user/session ownership and exact definition digests before planning any effect
Fail closed on missing evidence, another profile, legacy migration, live/unknown processes, mismatched source or unresolved operations
Specify digest-bound receipts, fencing, progress, uncertainty and explicit stopped-operation release without automatic retry or data deletion
No OS service, enrollment, existing configuration, checkout or remote target is changed
privacy: Neutral invented fixtures only. No credential/config contents, real host paths, remote access or OS service commands. Actual usage counters unavailable.
validation: Typed contract and cross-boundary renderer/ownership/recovery regression tests
Applicable fast checks, planner and required final CI
Review contract assumptions and explicitly retain real-device/OS/session acceptance limits

2026-11-10: 35 focused lifecycle/bootstrap/runtime tests pass, one platform skip; five lifecycle contract/CLI tests cover actual renderer, ownership and recovery joins. Typecheck/conventions and fast checks pass. Final CI pending; no service/device acceptance claimed.
escalation: Owner chooses the installation and pairing/service intent after reviewing the concrete contract; remote targets stay deferred
No execution adapter may infer ownership from a filename, receipt or process ID alone
